notes.subject: כמרימי על
notes.rationale: 'man i hautim yok' (raise/lift the yoke onto jaws, KJV/ASV) vs 'take off the yoke' (JPS/BSB) — same verb, opposite pastoral pictures.

notes.subject: חבלי אדם
notes.rationale: 'rop bilong man' (cords of a man, literal) vs 'human cords' i.e. humaneness/gentleness — most read it adverbially, 'as a man gently draws'.

notes.subject: ואט אליו אוכיל
notes.rationale: 'mi bent i go long em, mi kaikaivim em' — sudden shift to singular 'him' (Ephraim as one child); some repoint as 'I was to them as one who eases' or emend the verb.

notes.subject: לחי
notes.rationale: rendered 'maus' (mouth/jaw); Hebrew is the fleshy cheek or jawbone specifically.

translation: Long ol rop bilong man mi pulim ⟨i⟩ ol; long ol rop bilong lav; na mi kamap long ol olsem man i hautim ⟨את⟩ yok antap long ol maus bilong ol; na mi bent i go long em, na mi kaikaivim ⟨i⟩ em.
